atrabilious.oewn-01138769-s.why: Three book-only words in one short line - ornate, ailment and archaic - leave the learner with nothing to hold on to.

best-known.oewn-01378472-s.why: The note opens with the grammar term superlative and then leans on grandeur, a word met only in books.

preposterously.oewn-00388921-r.why: Indignant and repudiating are both rare words, and they carry the whole meaning of the note.

used.oewn-02505376-s.why: Participle is a grammar term the learner would have to look up, and 'landing colder for it' has no plain reading to fall back on.

adorable.oewn-01462677-s.why: The note starts with the grammar term superlative, which the learner cannot get past without looking it up.
